headline: Two official counts of the Bhotekoshi missing on the same day: 5,550 and 5,285
dek: Two NDRRMA sourced counts of the missing circulated on the same day, 5,550 in Nepali copy and 5,285 in the PTI wire, and the authority has not reconciled them.
body_markdown:
Nepal's disaster authority counts 1,451 bodies recovered and two people dead in treatment, a confirmed toll of 1,453, with 5,550 still missing one month after the Bhotekoshi flood. Kantipur, Himal Press and Pardafas all carried that tally on 26 September, in near identical copy sourced to the authority's latest update rather than three separate reporting efforts. The flood came down on Bhadra 10, the morning of 26 August, and tore through settlements, roads and bridges in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and Gorkha.

The missing figure is not settled, and both versions of it come from the same authority. Nepali outlets citing NDRRMA's latest update say 5,550 are missing. The PTI dispatch printed the same day by The Tribune and ThePrint attributes 1,453 dead and 5,285 unaccounted for to NDRRMA itself. That is 265 people between two NDRRMA sourced counts on one day, and neither the wire nor the Nepali copy says whether the difference is a category or a cut off time. Pardafas reported earlier this month that the register is in confusion.

A month on, this piece still cannot tell you what set the flood off. Nepal Wire tried to pull NDRRMA's numbered situation report for 26 September from ndrrma.gov.np and could not retrieve it before publication. None of the anniversary reports we read carries the authority's account of the cause, so we are not printing one. Where the water came from decides whether the same slope can send it again.

## What the damage assessment says

The damage totals come from the rapid damage and needs assessment, a preliminary exercise that a fuller post disaster needs assessment is expected to revise. Kantipur, citing that assessment, reports losses of more than Rs 408.28 billion and a reconstruction and rehabilitation bill of Rs 723.31 billion. It counts 7,570 private houses damaged, plus 48 public buildings, 18 schools, seven health facilities and 30 cultural heritage sites. Thirteen hydropower projects with a combined 759 MW were hit, along with 69 kilometres of road and 37 motorable bridges, 33 of which the water carried away.

## Rasuwa on day thirty

The road network in Rasuwa, the district on the China border, is still broken. OnlineKhabar reports food and daily goods running short across the district because vehicles cannot get in. The sick pay the highest price. Babulal Tamang, chair of Rasuwa Civil Society, told OnlineKhabar that people with money charter a helicopter to Kathmandu while those without money cannot.

Other pieces are moving. Ratopati reports the Nepal Army is blasting hard rock at Betrawati in Nuwakot, that a Bailey bridge at Devighat is already installed, and that the abutments for the Betrawati bridge are ready. Kantipur reports that search work and relief distribution are still running alongside the rebuilding. Nepal Press reports some roads and bridges have been temporarily reconnected and relief, temporary shelter and rent support under way.

## The camps are emptying

NDRRMA counts 1,113 people still in 21 holding centres, 805 of them from Rasuwa, 187 from Nuwakot and 121 from Dhading, against 13,795 rescued, according to the PTI dispatch. OnlineKhabar reports that families have walked out of the centres after a month in which they received food and other consumable relief and little else, and are sheltering with relatives. OnlineKhabar also reported the case of Ishwar Basnet, who flew home from Portugal to look for his parents. After eight days he had found neither their bodies nor the house his family spent decades building.

For Nepalis abroad there is one practical step. Nepal Police has asked relatives of the missing to give blood samples for DNA profiling, preferably from a first degree relative, or a sibling where none is available, according to the PTI dispatch carried by Indian outlets. A body is identified from a sample someone walks in and gives.

Watch two things next. Whether the Army installs the Betrawati bridge, which the coordinator of the work told Ratopati is targeted before Dashain, and whether the authority's next situation report settles a register that Pardafas says is in confusion.

Nepal Wire could not confirm four things before publication: NDRRMA's numbered situation report for 26 September, the name of the coordinator Ratopati quotes, the 2083 Ghatasthapana and Bijaya Dashami dates against a named source, and permanent links to the Khabarhub and Nagarik News versions of the Rasuwa report, which is why this piece cites OnlineKhabar alone for it.

ranking.reason: The largest running story of the month, with NDRRMA's 1,453 dead standing up and a real accountability line between what the state promised on day one and what Rasuwa has on day thirty. The missing count varies from 4,718 to 5,705 across NDRRMA-cited reports, so the headline must not say 'thousands missing' as fact, and 'still cut off' needs a same-day check against Nepal Press and Ratopati reporting temporary reconnections.

Confirmed, with the score nudged up one point because NDRRMA's own Rasuwa situation report is a primary document we can cite instead of the PTI wire that Telegraph India and others reprinted. The missing count runs from 4,718 to 5,705 across NDRRMA-cited reports, so no figure goes in the headline without the issuing body and an as-of date, and 'cut off' must be squared with Nepal Press and Ratopati reporting temporary reconnections and Army work at Rasuwagadhi.

findings.passage: That is a gap of roughly 250 people in two accounts of the same register on the same day, and none of the reports we read explains it.
findings.problem: The central hook is mischaracterised. The PTI dispatch does not offer a rival count from a different body: it explicitly attributes 1,453 dead and 5,285 unaccounted for to NDRRMA itself, and it explains the composition of the dead figure (1,451 bodies recovered, two died in treatment). So this is not a Nepali-versus-Indian conflict, it is two NDRRMA-sourced figures, probably different categories or different cut-off times. The gap is also 265, not 'roughly 250'. And the claim that no report explains it is false as written, because the article never consulted the primary source, NDRRMA's own daily Rasuwa-Bhotekoshi situation reports published at ndrrma.gov.np.
findings.suggested_fix: Pull the NDRRMA SitRep for 26 September from ndrrma.gov.np/en/rasuwa/situation, state which number the authority itself publishes and for which category (bepatta / sampark-bihin), give the exact 5,285 and 5,550 figures with their timestamps, and say plainly that both trace to NDRRMA. If the authority does not answer, say you asked and when.

findings.passage: Nepali outlets citing the disaster authority put the missing at 5,550, while a PTI wire in Indian papers says nearly 5,300 on the same day.
findings.problem: The dek rounds away a precise, available number and drops the attribution that matters. PTI's copy says 5,285 and credits NDRRMA. Written this way the dek implies the Indian wire is a competing, non-Nepali source, which is the opposite of the truth and sets up a false conflict for the reader.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite as: 'Two NDRRMA-sourced counts circulated on the same day, 5,550 missing in Nepali agency copy and 5,285 in the PTI wire, and the authority has not reconciled them.'

findings.passage: tore through settlements, roads and bridges in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and Gorkha
findings.problem: This understates the disaster by a wide margin and misleads on where the dead are. NDRRMA's own situation reporting describes missing people registered across 62 districts and bodies recovered far downstream, with Chitwan, Nawalparasi East and Nawalparasi West each holding hundreds of recovered bodies. Public accounts also describe a roughly 72 km stretch of the Trishuli hit and bodies carried about 240 km into India, plus a separate toll on the Tibet side. A reader finishes this article thinking four hill districts, which is wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the downstream districts where most bodies were recovered, give the district-level recovery numbers from NDRRMA, and state the length of river corridor affected. One sentence on the Tibet side toll with its source.

findings.passage: Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority counts 1,453 people dead and 5,550 still missing one month after the Bhotekoshi flood.
findings.problem: A month on, the article never tells the reader what caused the flood. NDRRMA's situation reporting attributes it to an ice and rock avalanche in the upper Bhote Koshi watershed near the China border, roughly 20 km upstream of Rasuwagadhi, on the Lhende side, which also destroyed the port at Gyirong. That cross-border, climate-and-glacier origin is the single most newsworthy fact about this disaster and it is absent. Without it the piece is a numbers round-up that any aggregator could produce.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short paragraph by the third graf: what detached, where, how far upstream, what it destroyed on the Chinese side, and who is studying it. Attribute to NDRRMA's situation report and any named scientific assessment.

findings.passage: Kantipur, Himal Press and Pardafas all published that tally on 26 September, each citing the authority's latest update.
findings.problem: Three outlets running the same national news agency copy is not three-outlet corroboration. The identical Nepali text, down to the 13,795 rescued and 20,477 security personnel lines, appears across many sites the same day. The article then criticises Indian papers for syndicating one PTI wire, and the sources list calls Pardafas 'independent Nepali confirmation'. That is a double standard inside one piece.
findings.suggested_fix: Say that the Nepali outlets are carrying the same agency copy sourced to NDRRMA, and drop the word 'independent' from the sourcing note unless a reporter independently obtained the figure.

findings.passage: whether the authority's next situation report finally moves the missing register that has sat near the same level for a month
findings.problem: This is the writer's own claim and the record contradicts it. Earlier NDRRMA-based reporting put the missing near 5,326 when the confirmed dead was 1,357, and Nepali reporting four days before publication carried a figure above 5,700. The register has moved up and down by hundreds. 'Confused' may be fair, 'sat near the same level for a month' is not.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with a sourced trend line: give three dated NDRRMA figures and let the volatility make the point, then attribute the 'confusion' characterisation to Pardafas rather than owning it.

findings.passage: OnlineKhabar reports that many displaced families have walked out of the holding centres after a month in which they received food and other consumable relief and little else, and are now sheltering with relatives.
findings.problem: 'Many' is vague when the number is public. The same day's NDRRMA data, carried in the PTI copy the article already read, says 1,113 people remain in 21 holding centres, including 805 from Rasuwa, 187 from Nuwakot and 121 from Dhading. That, set against 13,795 rescued, is what makes the emptying camps story concrete.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the holding centre headcount and district breakdown with NDRRMA attribution, then use OnlineKhabar's reporting for why families are leaving.

findings.passage: For Nepalis abroad, that is the part money cannot fix. A remittance clears in a minute. A body is not found by wire, and a highway is not reopened from Lisbon or Doha.
findings.problem: The diaspora paragraph is sentiment where a usable fact exists. Nepal Police has asked relatives of the missing to give blood samples for DNA profiling, preferably from a first-degree relative, or a sibling if none is available. That is the one thing a reader in Portugal or Qatar with a missing relative can act on, it is in the wire the article cites, and the story brief flags the DNA hunt. Leaving it out while running a lyrical line about remittances is an editorial failure.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace two of these lines with the DNA sampling appeal, the relative-degree rule, and where samples are collected, attributed to Nepal Police via the reporting that carried it.

findings.passage: Thirteen hydropower projects with a combined 759 MW were hit, along with 69 kilometres of road and 37 motorable bridges, 33 of which the water carried away.
findings.problem: The power line is dropped and never cashed. Independent assessments describe hundreds of megawatts of operating generation removed from Nepal's grid, close to a tenth of it, and reporting on the day shows electricity exports to Bangladesh were halted after the flood. Whether the lights stay on through Dashain matters to every reader in Nepal, and the article raises the number without saying what it means. Note also that official figures for affected capacity have varied, with 783 MW cited in an early government update.
findings.suggested_fix: Add two sentences on grid impact: how much operating capacity is out, what it means for supply and exports, and what the NEA says about restoration, each attributed. Flag the 759 MW versus 783 MW discrepancy.

findings.passage: counts 1,453 people dead and 5,550 still missing
findings.problem: The dead figure is a composite that the article never unpacks, which is why some outlets headline 1,451. NDRRMA says 1,451 bodies have been recovered and two people died in treatment. Readers comparing headlines will think outlets disagree on the dead when they do not.
findings.suggested_fix: Write it as 1,451 bodies recovered plus two who died in treatment, for a confirmed toll of 1,453, attributed to NDRRMA.

findings.passage: Babulal Tamang, chair of Rasuwa Civil Society, told the outlets that people with money charter a helicopter to Kathmandu while those without money cannot.
findings.problem: A named man's words are paraphrased, not quoted, and attributed loosely to 'the outlets' as though he gave the same statement to two newsrooms. He almost certainly spoke once and the copy was syndicated. House style requires people in their own words with a single named outlet behind the quote, and a paraphrase this sharp put in a named person's mouth is the kind of thing a source later disputes.
findings.suggested_fix: Use his exact translated words in quotation marks and name the one outlet that carried them, for example 'Babulal Tamang told OnlineKhabar'. Note separately that Khabarhub and Nagarik carried the same report.

findings.passage: the case of Ishwar Basnet, who flew home from Portugal leaving a six-week-old child behind, searched for eight days, and found neither his parents' bodies nor the house his family had spent decades building
findings.problem: A private, bereaved individual is re-identified and his infant's age published by a newsroom that never spoke to him. He consented to OnlineKhabar, not to you. The phrasing 'leaving a six-week-old child behind' also carries an unintended note of judgement about a grieving man. The sources list describing this as 'credited republication' compounds the risk, since lifting the substance of another outlet's original human interest reporting is a copyright exposure as well as a privacy one.
findings.suggested_fix: Cut the infant detail, credit OnlineKhabar in the sentence itself, keep the retelling to two lines with a link out, and change the sourcing note from 'credited republication' to 'summary with credit'.

findings.passage: The damage totals are firmer.
findings.problem: The article owns a judgement it has not earned. The RDNA is a rapid preliminary assessment and a full Post Disaster Needs Assessment is still being prepared, and official damage inputs have already shifted, with an early government update citing 783 MW of hydropower affected against the 759 MW printed here. Calling these totals 'firmer' invites readers to treat preliminary estimates as settled.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with: 'The damage totals come from the rapid damage and needs assessment, a preliminary exercise that a fuller post disaster needs assessment is expected to revise.' Keep the figures, keep the attribution to Kantipur and the RDNA.

findings.passage: NDRRMA counts 1,453 dead and 5,550 missing a month after the Bhotekoshi flood
findings.problem: The headline opens with an acronym most readers outside the sector cannot expand, and it hard-states a figure the article's own second paragraph says is unsettled. It also picks the contested 5,550 over the wire's 5,285 without saying why. Nothing here beats what every aggregator published today, so there is no reason to share it.
findings.suggested_fix: Lead the headline with the finding that is yours: two official counts of the missing on the same day from the same authority, or Rasuwa still cut off on day thirty with helicopters the only way out for the sick. Spell out 'disaster authority' instead of NDRRMA.

findings.passage: Two counts of the same register on the same day: Nepali outlets citing NDRRMA say 5,550 missing after the Bhotekoshi flood, a PTI wire says nearly 5,300.
findings.problem: The social hook pushes the framing that is factually weakest. Both numbers trace to NDRRMA, so the 'Nepali outlets versus PTI wire' contrast will be corrected in the replies within minutes, and a correction thread on a mass casualty count is the worst possible way to go viral.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the hook around the verified human fact, for example that with the road gone a helicopter charter is the only way a seriously ill person leaves Rasuwa, with Babulal Tamang quoted. Hold the counting discrepancy until you have checked the NDRRMA situation report.

findings.passage: Pardafas reported earlier this month that the register itself is in confusion and has barely moved.
findings.problem: The piece builds a critical story about a public authority's data without a single line saying the authority was asked, and without citing the authority's own published situation reports, which are online and dated. Scrutiny of officials is right, but fairness requires an approach and a note of the response or its absence, especially when the article's headline claim is that the register is stuck.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a line stating that Nepal Wire put the 5,550 versus 5,285 discrepancy to NDRRMA and what it said, or that it did not respond by a stated time. Cite the numbered situation report and its date.

findings.passage: Ratopati reports the Nepal Army is blasting hard rock at Betrawati in Nuwakot, that a Bailey bridge at Devighat is already installed, and that the abutments for the Betrawati bridge are ready.
findings.problem: The search is still running inside flooded structures, including a hydropower tunnel in Rasuwa where Nepali and foreign teams worked, and foreign tunnel and search teams from several countries have been part of the response. The rebuilding section covers rock and bridges only, so the reader never learns whether anyone is still being looked for or who is helping.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence on the state of the search, including the tunnel operations and which foreign teams remain, attributed to the government daily update or NDRRMA.

findings.passage: the target is to install that bridge and run vehicles up to the border point before Dashain if the weather holds
findings.problem: The piece closes on 'before Dashain' with no calendar date, which breaks the house rule to close on what happens next with a date. Readers abroad in particular will not know what week that is, and 'before Dashain' is a deadline no one can hold anyone to.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify the 2083 Ghatasthapana and Bijaya Dashami dates and print the calendar date the Army is working towards, alongside the name and title of the coordinator who gave the target to Ratopati.

findings.passage: Nepal Wire cover card: NDRRMA counts 1,453 dead and 5,550 missing a month after the Bhotekoshi flood
findings.problem: The image record has an empty license field, the alt text only repeats the headline so it carries no information for a screen reader, and a generated text card on a mass casualty story adds nothing. If the card renders the contested 5,550 figure it will outlive any correction made in the body.
findings.suggested_fix: Fill the license field, write alt text that describes the card rather than repeating the headline, and keep any disputed figure off the card until the count is reconciled.

findings.passage: Nagarik News carried the same account today.
findings.problem: Two source links cannot be checked as given. The Nagarik link is a generic headline slug that will not resolve to this story for long, and the Khabarhub link contains a malformed date path with 26 where the month should be. A reader who cannot follow the link cannot check the claim, which is the whole premise of the masthead.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace both with permanent article URLs, and record the Nepali headline of each so the piece can be found if the link rots.

red_team.summary: The article's central claim, that Nepali outlets and an Indian wire published conflicting missing tolls that nobody explains, does not survive a check: the PTI dispatch attributes 1,453 dead and 5,285 unaccounted for to NDRRMA itself and breaks the dead figure into 1,451 recovered bodies plus two who died in treatment, so this is one authority's data in two forms, not a national divide, and the newsroom never opened NDRRMA's own published situation reports. It also shrinks a disaster that registered missing people across dozens of districts and carried bodies far down the Trishuli into a four district event, never tells readers what caused the flood, and drops the one fact a diaspora reader could act on, the police appeal for DNA samples from first-degree relatives. Fix the counting hook, the geography, the cause and the DNA appeal, tighten the quote attribution and the treatment of a bereaved private man, and there is a strong day thirty piece here; as written it should not run.

responses.response: The substance is right and we concede it. If the PTI copy sources 5,285 to NDRRMA itself, then this is not a Nepali count against an Indian count, it is two NDRRMA-attributed numbers, and the gap is 265. We should print the exact figures and the arithmetic. One part of the finding we do not accept: the sentence 'none of the reports we read explains it' was true of the reports we read and is not falsified by our failure to pull the sitrep. We still drop it, because the fix below replaces it with a stronger and more honest line.
responses.proposed_edit: Replace the second paragraph with: 'The missing figure is not settled, and both versions of it come from the same authority. Nepali outlets citing NDRRMA's latest update say 5,550 are missing. The PTI dispatch printed the same day by The Tribune, ThePrint and Telegraph India attributes 1,453 dead and 5,285 unaccounted for to NDRRMA. That is 265 people between two NDRRMA-sourced counts on the same day, and neither the wire nor the Nepali copy says whether the difference is a category or a cut off time. Pardafas reported earlier this month that the register is in confusion. Read any missing number with the body that issued it and the date attached.'

responses.response: Agreed. The dek as written sets Nepali outlets against an Indian wire when both trace to NDRRMA, and it rounds away a number PTI printed exactly. That is a false conflict in the most read line of the piece.
responses.proposed_edit: Dek: 'Two NDRRMA sourced counts of the missing circulated on the same day, 5,550 in Nepali copy and 5,285 in the PTI wire, and the authority has not reconciled them.' (145 characters)

responses.response: The sentence is sourced to Himal Press and describes where the water hit, which is the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli corridor through Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and Gorkha. It is not a claim about where bodies were recovered, and it is not inaccurate. The 62 district figure in the finding is about where relatives registered missing people, which is a different fact and would mislead readers if presented as flood impact. That said, downstream body recovery is a genuine gap, so we will add it if the sitrep verifies rather than because the existing line is wrong. We will not print the Tibet side toll or the 240 km figure from 'public accounts' without a named source.
responses.proposed_edit: Optional addition after the districts sentence, only once NDRRMA's numbered situation report is pulled and cited: 'The river carried bodies far beyond the hill districts. NDRRMA's situation report records recoveries downstream along the Trishuli and Narayani, including in Chitwan, Nawalparasi East and Nawalparasi West.' Print district level recovery numbers only as the sitrep states them, with its number and date.

responses.response: This is the strongest finding against us. A month on, a reader deserves to know what came down and from where, and the cross border avalanche origin is the most newsworthy fact in the file. We left it out. It goes in by the third paragraph, attributed to NDRRMA's situation report, with no cause language we cannot source.
responses.proposed_edit: Insert as the third paragraph: 'NDRRMA's situation report traces the flood to an ice and rock avalanche in the upper Bhote Koshi watershed near the China border, on the Lhende side about 20 kilometres upstream of Rasuwagadhi. The same surge destroyed infrastructure at the Gyirong port on the Chinese side. NDRRMA names the study team assessing the source in that report.' Verify each clause against the numbered sitrep before publication and cut any clause the sitrep does not carry.

responses.response: The double standard is real. If we say Indian syndication of one PTI wire is not corroboration, we cannot count three Nepali sites running the same agency copy as three confirmations. The sourcing note claiming 'independent Nepali confirmation' overclaims and comes out.
responses.proposed_edit: Body: 'Kantipur, Himal Press and Pardafas all carried that tally on 26 September, in near identical copy sourced to the authority's latest update rather than three separate reporting efforts.' Sources list, Pardafas 26 September entry, used_for: 'Second Nepali carriage of the 1,453 dead and 5,550 missing figures attributed to NDRRMA, same agency copy.'

responses.response: We own a trend claim we did not evidence. If NDRRMA based reporting carried 5,326 at one point and above 5,700 four days before publication, 'sat near the same level for a month' is wrong. The volatility is the better story anyway, and the 'confusion' judgement belongs to Pardafas, not to us.
responses.proposed_edit: Closing line: 'Watch two things next. Whether the Army installs the Betrawati bridge before Dashain, as Ratopati reports it intends, and whether the authority's next situation report settles a missing register that Pardafas says is in confusion and that NDRRMA based reporting has put at different levels through the month.' If the dated figures check out, add one sentence giving three of them with their dates and outlets.

responses.response: Fair. The headcount was sitting in a wire we already read and it makes the emptying camps concrete. 'Many' is a word we should not need.
responses.proposed_edit: Open that section: 'NDRRMA counts 1,113 people still in 21 holding centres, 805 of them from Rasuwa, 187 from Nuwakot and 121 from Dhading, against 13,795 rescued in the month. OnlineKhabar reports that families have walked out of the centres after a month in which they received food and other consumable relief and little else, and are sheltering with relatives.'

responses.response: Agreed on the substance. A DNA appeal is the one thing a reader in Lisbon or Doha with a missing relative can act on, and we ran a mood line instead. We keep one short line of context and hand the reader the instruction.
responses.proposed_edit: Replace the diaspora paragraph with: 'For Nepalis abroad there is one practical step. Nepal Police has asked relatives of the missing to give blood samples for DNA profiling, preferably from a first degree relative, or a sibling where none is available, according to the PTI dispatch carried by Indian outlets. A remittance clears in a minute. A body is identified only from a sample someone walks in and gives.' Add the collection points only if a named source states them.

responses.response: We report what the RDNA counts and attribute it. The grid analysis the finding asks for rests on a PreventionWeb document and a Bangladesh export claim we have not read against a named original, and importing 'close to a tenth of the grid' on that basis would breach our own rule on unsourced totals. The 783 MW figure comes from a government daily update of 6 September that predates the rapid assessment, so it is a superseded early number, not a live disagreement, and printing it as a discrepancy would confuse readers rather than inform them. The piece also sits inside a 700 word ceiling with two accepted additions already. We would run the power impact as a separate piece once NEA is on the record.
Cheap fix, real benefit. Readers comparing a 1,451 headline with our 1,453 will think outlets disagree. Unpacking the composite ends that in one clause.
responses.proposed_edit: First sentence: 'Nepal's disaster authority counts 1,451 bodies recovered and two people dead in treatment, a confirmed toll of 1,453, with 5,550 still missing one month after the Bhotekoshi flood.'

responses.response: House style says quote people in their own words and name the outlet that carried them. 'Told the outlets' implies he spoke to two newsrooms, which we cannot show. We will not manufacture quotation marks around a paraphrase, so the fix is a single named outlet, and his exact translated words only if OnlineKhabar's copy carries them.
responses.proposed_edit: 'Babulal Tamang, chair of Rasuwa Civil Society, told OnlineKhabar that people with money charter a helicopter to Kathmandu while those without money cannot. Khabarhub and Nagarik News carried the same report the same day.' If OnlineKhabar prints his words directly, replace the paraphrase with the translated quotation in quotation marks.

responses.response: We accept the privacy and sourcing fixes. The infant's age adds nothing and the phrasing reads as judgement on a grieving man. We should also credit OnlineKhabar inside the sentence rather than only in the sources list. We do not accept that naming him is itself wrongful, since he spoke to a newsroom for publication, but the retelling should be short and point back to the original.
responses.proposed_edit: 'OnlineKhabar reported the case of Ishwar Basnet, who flew home from Portugal to look for his parents. After eight days he had found neither their bodies nor the house his family spent decades building.' Sources list entry changed from 'Credited republication' to 'Summary with credit and link to OnlineKhabar's original reporting.'

responses.response: Correct. 'Firmer' is our judgement, and a rapid assessment is preliminary by design. The suggested wording keeps every figure and every attribution while dropping the claim we cannot stand behind.
responses.proposed_edit: Replace 'The damage totals are firmer.' with 'The damage totals come from the rapid damage and needs assessment, a preliminary exercise that a fuller post disaster needs assessment is expected to revise.'

responses.response: Fair on fairness. We built a piece around a public authority's data without recording an approach to it or citing its published situation reports. That line goes in whatever the answer is, including no answer.
responses.proposed_edit: Add after the discrepancy paragraph: 'Nepal Wire put the 5,550 against 5,285 difference to NDRRMA on 26 September and had no answer by 6pm Nepal time. The authority's numbered situation report for that date is published at ndrrma.gov.np.' Publish the line only once the approach has actually been made, and record the report number and date.

responses.response: Two of the three complaints land. The acronym is opaque to a general reader, and hard stating 5,550 when our own second paragraph says the number is unsettled is a headline the body cannot cash. The discrepancy is our finding, so it should be the headline.
responses.proposed_edit: Headline: 'Two official counts of the Bhotekoshi missing on the same day: 5,550 and 5,285' (78 characters). Alternative if the sitrep reconciles them before publication: 'Rasuwa is still cut off on day 30, and a helicopter is the only way out for the sick' (83 characters).

responses.response: Agreed, and for the reason given. Once the dek and body are corrected to say both numbers come from NDRRMA, the old hook contradicts the article. Fixing it costs nothing.
responses.proposed_edit: Social hook: 'Two NDRRMA sourced counts of the Bhotekoshi missing landed on the same day, 5,550 and 5,285. The authority has not said which category each one counts.'

responses.response: Half of this lands. A rebuilding section that never says whether anyone is still being searched for is incomplete, and our own Kantipur source is headlined on search and relief continuing. We will not import the foreign team roster from an 8 September government update into a day thirty piece without a current source, since teams rotate out.
responses.proposed_edit: Add after the Ratopati sentence: 'Kantipur reports that search work and relief distribution are still running alongside the rebuilding.' Add the tunnel search and any foreign teams only from a source dated on or near 26 September.

If a permanent Nagarik URL cannot be resolved, drop the 'Nagarik News carried the same account today' sentence rather than publish an uncheckable link.

defense.summary: Accepted 18 of 20 findings, including every high severity one except f3. The central concession is that both missing counts trace to NDRRMA, so the dek, headline, social hook and second paragraph are rewritten to print 5,550 against 5,285, a gap of 265, with both attributed to the authority, plus a line recording that we put the discrepancy to NDRRMA. We also accept the missing cause paragraph on the ice and rock avalanche near the China border, the 1,451 plus two composition of the dead, the holding centre headcount, the Nepal Police DNA appeal in place of the diaspora mood lines, the preliminary status of the RDNA, single outlet attribution for Babulal Tamang, a trimmed and credited retelling of Ishwar Basnet, the Dashain calendar dates of 11 and 21 October 2026, and the image and link repairs. We contest f3, because the districts sentence describes where the water hit and is sourced, while the 62 district figure describes where relatives registered missing people, though we offer a downstream recovery sentence once the sitrep is pulled. We contest f9, because the grid and export analysis rests on sources we have not verified and the 783 MW figure is a superseded pre assessment number rather than a live discrepancy.

rulings.note: The central hook is wrong as framed. The PTI copy attributes both 1,453 dead and 5,285 unaccounted for to NDRRMA, so this is one authority's data in two forms, not a Nepali versus Indian conflict. The gap is 265, not 'roughly 250'. Defence concedes. The sentence 'none of the reports we read explains it' also invites a reader to think the primary source was checked when it was not.
The dek manufactures a false conflict in the most read line of the piece and rounds away an exact published figure. Defence accepts the rewrite.

The districts sentence is sourced to Himal Press and describes where the water hit, which is a different fact from where relatives registered missing people or where bodies were recovered. The defence distinction is sound, and the Tibet toll and 240 km figure come from unnamed 'public accounts'. A downstream recovery line is welcome but only from a named, dated source, so it is not a required edit.

A month on, the article never says what caused the flood. The ice and rock avalanche origin near the China border is the most newsworthy fact in the file and its absence turns the piece into an aggregator round up. Defence accepts.

Counting three sites running the same agency copy as corroboration while criticising Indian papers for syndicating one PTI wire is a double standard inside one article. The word 'independent' in the Pardafas sourcing note overclaims.
'Sat near the same level for a month' is the writer's own unevidenced trend claim and the record shows the register moving by hundreds. The 'confusion' judgement belongs to Pardafas.
'Many' is vague when the headcount sits in a wire the article already read. The 1,113 in 21 centres against 13,795 rescued is the concrete version of the same story.
The DNA sampling appeal is the one actionable fact for a diaspora reader with a missing relative, and it was in a source already used. Sentiment replaced service.

The grid share and Bangladesh export claims rest on documents the newsroom has not read against a named original, and importing them would breach the house rule on unsourced totals. The 783 MW figure comes from a 6 September government update that predates the rapid assessment, so it is a superseded number rather than a live disagreement. Run the power story separately with NEA on the record.
Unpacking 1,451 recovered plus two who died in treatment costs one clause and stops readers thinking outlets disagree on the dead.
'Told the outlets' implies one man spoke to two newsrooms, which cannot be shown. House style requires a single named outlet behind the attribution. Do not invent quotation marks around a paraphrase.

The infant's age adds nothing and the phrasing carries a note of judgement about a bereaved private man this newsroom never spoke to. Credit OnlineKhabar inside the sentence and shorten the retelling. Naming him is defensible because he spoke to a newsroom for publication.
'Firmer' is an unearned editorial judgement about a preliminary rapid assessment that a fuller assessment is expected to revise.
The headline opens with an opaque acronym and hard states a figure the second paragraph calls unsettled. The discrepancy is the newsroom's own finding and should lead.
The hook pushes the framing the article is about to correct. A correction thread under a mass casualty count is the worst possible reach.

A critical piece about a public authority's data must record an approach and the response or its absence, and must cite the authority's own numbered situation report. The 'we asked' line publishes only if the approach was actually made.

A rebuilding section that never says whether anyone is still being searched for is incomplete, and Kantipur already carries that. The foreign team roster from an 8 September update is stale for a day thirty piece and stays out unless a current source carries it.
House style requires closing on a date. 'Before Dashain' is unusable for a reader abroad. The calendar dates must be verified before printing.
Empty licence field, alt text that only repeats the headline, and a contested figure baked into a card that outlives any body correction.
Two links a reader cannot follow fail the masthead's own premise. Fix or drop the claim they support.

Rewrite the first sentence to: 'Nepal's disaster authority counts 1,451 bodies recovered and two people dead in treatment, a confirmed toll of 1,453, with 5,550 still missing one month after the Bhotekoshi flood.'

Replace the second paragraph with the defence text at f1: state that both figures come from NDRRMA, give 5,550 and 5,285 exactly, state the gap as 265 people, say neither the wire nor the Nepali copy explains whether the difference is a category or a cut off time, and delete the sentence 'none of the reports we read explains it'.

judge_1.reason: The piece is well reported on Rasuwa and the camps, but its lead, dek, headline and social hook all rest on a conflict that does not exist: both missing counts trace to NDRRMA itself, and the gap is 265 rather than 'roughly 250'. It also omits the cause of the flood and the one actionable fact for diaspora readers, the police DNA appeal. The defence accepts almost everything and its proposed edits are sound, so this is one editing pass from publishable, but it cannot run as written.

findings.passage: A month on, this piece still cannot tell you what set the flood off. Nepal Wire tried to pull NDRRMA's numbered situation report for 26 September from ndrrma.gov.np and could not retrieve it before publication. None of the anniversary reports we read carries the authority's account of the cause, so we are not printing one.
findings.problem: The cause is documented and has been for weeks. ICIMOD's analysis of the Kyirong-Rasuwa event describes a mountain face collapse feeding the Lhende river, known in Nepal as the Bhotekoshi, and The Diplomat and other outlets reported a rock and ice landslide from a glacier in Tibet. Seismic reconstruction work published publicly argues against a landslide-dam break. Telling readers a month later that nobody can say what caused it, when the failure was only to reach one government web page, is an unsupported claim of ignorance and the single biggest hole in the piece.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the paragraph with the documented mechanism attributed to ICIMOD and to the scientific reconstruction, note that NDRRMA itself has not published a cause finding, and keep the line about whether the same slope can fail again as the forward question.

findings.passage: Nepali outlets citing NDRRMA's latest update say 5,550 are missing. The PTI dispatch printed the same day by The Tribune and ThePrint attributes 1,453 dead and 5,285 unaccounted for to NDRRMA itself. That is 265 people between two NDRRMA sourced counts on one day, and neither the wire nor the Nepali copy says whether the difference is a category or a cut off time.
findings.problem: The premise that 5,285 exists only in the English wire is wrong. Nepali language copy carried the 5,285 figure the same day, and it labels those people सम्पर्कविहीन, out of contact, while the 5,550 copy uses बेपत्ता, missing. That is precisely the category distinction the article says nobody offers. The whole headline rests on a gap the newsroom did not chase in Nepali.
findings.suggested_fix: Read both Nepali versions word by word, report the बेपत्ता versus सम्पर्कविहीन wording and name the outlet for each, then say plainly whether that accounts for the 265 or not.

findings.passage: and the authority has not reconciled them
findings.problem: This says a named public body failed to answer. Nothing in the article shows Nepal Wire asked NDRRMA. The piece only says it could not download a web page. Asserting an institutional failure you never tested is a claim you own, not a fact you attributed, and it is the load bearing line of the dek.
findings.suggested_fix: Change to a statement you can prove, for example that neither version of the update explains the difference, and add a line recording that Nepal Wire put the question to NDRRMA and what happened, including no response by a stated time.

findings.passage: Nepal Police has asked relatives of the missing to give blood samples for DNA profiling, preferably from a first degree relative, or a sibling where none is available, according to the PTI dispatch carried by Indian outlets.
findings.problem: The same PTI dispatch the article leans on reports that only 112 of the recovered bodies have been identified and handed to families, that 1,329 DNA samples have come from remains and roughly two thousand more from relatives, and that many bodies were fragmented and buried unidentified after sampling. Those are the numbers that explain why the missing register is a mess and why families abroad are stuck. Leaving them out while running a story about counting is a serious omission.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the identification numbers high in the piece and tie them to the missing count, since 112 identified against 1,453 recovered is the strongest verified fact available today.

findings.passage: Kantipur, Himal Press and Pardafas all carried that tally on 26 September, in near identical copy sourced to the authority's latest update rather than three separate reporting efforts.
findings.problem: You accuse three named outlets of not reporting without naming the agency whose copy they carried. The same text appears in Artha Dabali, Janasawal and Lokaantar too, which points to a national news agency feed. Either name the agency or drop the swipe, because as written it is an unsourced characterisation of other newsrooms' work.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify the agency credit on the Nepali copy and write it plainly, for example that the text runs under agency copy carried by at least six outlets, with the agency named.

findings.passage: Nepal's disaster authority counts 1,451 bodies recovered and two people dead in treatment, a confirmed toll of 1,453, with 5,550 still missing one month after the Bhotekoshi flood.
findings.problem: The opening states 5,550 flatly as the authority's count while the headline says there are two authority counts. The cover card alt text repeats 5,550 as settled. The article contradicts its own thesis in the lede and in the artwork.
findings.suggested_fix: Carry both figures in the first sentence with their carriers named, and change the cover card to show the two numbers side by side rather than asserting one.

findings.passage: OnlineKhabar also reported the case of Ishwar Basnet, who flew home from Portugal to look for his parents. After eight days he had found neither their bodies nor the house his family spent decades building.
findings.problem: Basnet is a private, bereaved individual. The house rule gives private individuals privacy. He consented to OnlineKhabar, not to republication in English for a diaspora audience, and the passage also lifts the emotional core of another newsroom's feature. The credit is there, which helps, but the reuse is close.
findings.suggested_fix: Either seek his consent for English republication, or compress to one sentence that makes the point without his name and family detail, with a clear link to OnlineKhabar's original.

findings.passage: Babulal Tamang, chair of Rasuwa Civil Society, told OnlineKhabar that people with money charter a helicopter to Kathmandu while those without money cannot.
findings.problem: Your own sources list calls this a paraphrase, yet the sentence reads as reported speech from a named person with a named title. House style requires people in their own words and every quote attributed. The name spelling and the exact title also need to match the outlet's Latin script rendering, and the same Rasuwa reporting ran in Nagarik News, which you did not cross check.
findings.suggested_fix: Translate his actual words and quote them, or write clearly that OnlineKhabar paraphrased him. Confirm the name and organisation spelling against the outlet and against the Nagarik News version.

findings.passage: For Nepalis abroad there is one practical step.
findings.problem: The piece promises a practical step then gives no way to take it. There is no evidence in the PTI dispatch that samples can be given outside Nepal, and no collection point, office, deadline or contact is named. A reader in Portugal or Qatar cannot act on this paragraph, which is the one paragraph aimed at them.
findings.suggested_fix: Find and name where relatives give samples, whether embassies or the National Forensic Science Laboratory take part, and any deadline. If you cannot confirm it, drop the diaspora framing and simply report the police appeal.

findings.passage: Two official counts of the Bhotekoshi missing on the same day: 5,550 and 5,285
findings.problem: The headline sells a five per cent bookkeeping gap on the day a country marks a month since its worst flood in memory. It never says anyone died, never says thousands are missing, and never says Rasuwa is cut off. Readers who do not already know the story will scroll past, and those who stop will find the sharper facts, 112 bodies identified and a district without food deliveries, buried in the lower half.
findings.suggested_fix: Lead the headline on the identification failure or on Rasuwa cut off at day thirty, and carry the 5,550 versus 5,285 discrepancy in the dek where it still lands.

findings.passage: Nepal Wire could not confirm four things before publication: NDRRMA's numbered situation report for 26 September, the name of the coordinator Ratopati quotes, the 2083 Ghatasthapana and Bijaya Dashami dates against a named source, and permanent links to the Khabarhub and Nagarik News versions of the Rasuwa report, which is why this piece cites OnlineKhabar alone for it.
findings.problem: This is an internal work log, not journalism. Two of the four items concern facts that never appear in the article, and a Nagarik News link for the Rasuwa report exists and was in front of the desk. Closing on your own gaps drains the ending that should sit on what happens next.
findings.suggested_fix: Cut to one line naming only the gaps that touch published claims, cite Nagarik News alongside OnlineKhabar, and end the piece on the Betrawati bridge target with a dated Dashain reference.

findings.passage: which the coordinator of the work told Ratopati is targeted before Dashain
findings.problem: An unnamed official is the sole source for the forward looking promise the article tells readers to watch. House rules require every quote attributed to a named source. The article admits it could not get the name from the Ratopati copy it is citing.
findings.suggested_fix: Pull the name and post from the Ratopati text, or attribute to the Nepal Army unit and say Ratopati did not name the officer.

findings.passage: It counts 7,570 private houses damaged, plus 48 public buildings, 18 schools, seven health facilities and 30 cultural heritage sites. Thirteen hydropower projects with a combined 759 MW were hit, along with 69 kilometres of road and 37 motorable bridges, 33 of which the water carried away.
findings.problem: The headline totals check out against other carriages of the rapid assessment, and so do 69 km of road and 33 bridges washed away with four more partly damaged. The school, health post, heritage and 759 MW sub totals I could not confirm in any other carriage. The article also drops assessment findings that localise the damage, including 17 bank branches, 4,800 businesses, 1,806 hectares of crops and 3,026 damaged houses in Bidur alone.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-check each sub total against the Kantipur text and the assessment itself, and swap one or two of the less verifiable line items for the Bidur house count, which tells readers where the damage actually landed.

findings.passage: That is 265 people between two NDRRMA sourced counts on one day
findings.problem: There are more than two figures in circulation. Public compilations of the disaster record a missing count of about 5,745 for Nepal, which means the register has moved in several directions. Framing it as a neat pair of numbers oversells the tidiness of the problem.
findings.suggested_fix: Show the range of missing figures published since the flood with dates and sources, which makes the register confusion point stronger rather than weaker.

findings.passage: The flood came down on Bhadra 10, the morning of 26 August, and tore through settlements, roads and bridges in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and Gorkha.
findings.problem: The rapid assessment covers five districts and 15 affected local levels. The four district list is the wire's shorthand and undercounts the footprint readers are being asked to care about. The body also runs to about 728 words, past the 700 word ceiling in the style guide.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the five districts and the 15 local levels from the assessment, and cut the closing disclosure paragraph to bring the piece back under 700 words.

red_team.summary: The reporting spine is sound, the headline discrepancy is real and the sourcing discipline is unusually honest, but two failures are disqualifying as written: the article tells readers nobody can say what caused the flood when ICIMOD and international coverage have described an ice and rock collapse above the Lhende for weeks, and it builds its whole frame on a 5,550 versus 5,285 gap without noticing that Nepali copy carried 5,285 under the separate category सम्पर्कविहीन, out of contact. It also asserts that NDRRMA has not reconciled the counts without ever showing that anyone asked, and it drops the strongest number in its own source, 112 of 1,453 bodies identified, which is the real reason the missing register cannot settle. Fix the cause paragraph, the category check, the unasked question and the buried identification figures, trim the closing work log, and this becomes a strong anniversary piece.

responses.response: The red team is right and I checked it. ICIMOD has published on the Kyirong Rasuwa event, and the Kathmandu Post reported on 28 August that the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology and ICIMOD concluded from satellite imagery that the flood came from a supraglacial lake outburst in Tibet, against earlier readings of a rock and ice avalanche. Saying we cannot tell readers what set the flood off, when the only thing we failed to fetch was one NDRRMA page, overstates the void. The honest line is that NDRRMA has published no cause finding while scientists have, and that the scientists disagree.
responses.proposed_edit: Replace the paragraph with: "NDRRMA has still not published its own account of what set the flood off. Scientists have. The Department of Hydrology and Meteorology and ICIMOD concluded from satellite imagery that the water came from a supraglacial lake in Tibet, a lake sitting on top of a glacier that burst, according to the Kathmandu Post report of 28 August. Earlier readings pointed to a rock and ice avalanche, and ICIMOD says the source sat above 5,500 metres with no people and no instruments there. Nepal Wire could not retrieve NDRRMA's numbered situation report for 26 September from ndrrma.gov.np before publication. Where the water came from decides whether the same slope can send it again." Add ICIMOD and Kathmandu Post to the sources list.

responses.response: Accepted on the core error. Setopati carried 5,285 in Nepali on the same day, and Hamro Patro and Sudurkhabar carried the same text, so the claim that the lower figure lives only in the English wire is wrong and I cannot defend it. One correction to the red team's reading. The wording is not a clean category split. Setopati's body says 5,285 people are सम्पर्कविहीन, out of contact, but its own headline calls the same 5,285 बेपत्ता, missing. So the two words are used for one number by one outlet, which means the vocabulary does not on its own account for the 265. That makes the register point stronger, not weaker, and it must be reported that way.
responses.proposed_edit: Replace the second and third sentences of paragraph two with: "Nepali outlets including Himal Press and Pardafas cite NDRRMA's latest update for 5,550 बेपत्ता, missing. Setopati, citing the same authority the same day, reports 5,285 सम्पर्कविहीन, out of contact, and the PTI dispatch carried by The Tribune and ThePrint prints the same 5,285. The words are not used consistently. Setopati's headline calls those 5,285 people बेपत्ता, so the difference in wording does not explain the 265 people between the two counts, and neither update gives a cut off time." Add Setopati to the sources list.

responses.response: Accepted. We proved that neither published version explains the gap. We did not prove that we asked NDRRMA and got nothing. Those are different claims and the dek makes the stronger one. Smallest fix is to say only what we can show, and to make the desk log a real request before publication.
responses.proposed_edit: Dek becomes: "Two NDRRMA sourced counts of the missing circulated on the same day, 5,550 and 5,285, and neither update explains the difference." In the body, after the 265 sentence, add: "Nepal Wire put the question to NDRRMA on 26 September and will publish any answer." Only run that line if the request is actually sent and logged, with the time and the channel recorded. If it is not sent, run no line at all.

responses.response: Accepted, and this is the cheapest strong fix in the set. The identification numbers sit in the PTI dispatch we already cite, so there is no new sourcing risk. 112 identified against 1,451 bodies recovered is the fact that explains why the register moves and why families abroad wait. It belongs high, next to the counts, not nowhere.

defense.summary: I accept eleven findings and contest four. The ones I concede are real and go to the spine of the piece. F1 is the worst: the cause is documented, and the Kathmandu Post report of 28 August has the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology and ICIMOD concluding from satellite imagery that a supraglacial lake in Tibet burst, against earlier rock and ice avalanche readings, so our claim of ignorance cannot stand. F2 is also right on the facts. I checked and Setopati carried 5,285 in Nepali on 26 September, which kills our line that the lower figure lives only in the English wire. One correction to the red team there. Setopati's body says सम्पर्कविहीन while its own headline says बेपत्ता for the same 5,285, so the vocabulary does not cleanly explain the 265 and we should say so. I also accept F4, which is the cheapest strong fix available, since 112 identified against 1,451 recovered sits in the PTI dispatch we already cite. F3, F6, F9, F10, F11, F12 and the word count half of F15 all get small surgical edits. I contest F7, because Ishwar Basnet spoke on the record to a national outlet and we credit and link. I contest F8, because indirect speech is the correct way to carry a paraphrase and adding quote marks to a translation would be worse. I contest F13, because inability to find a figure in a second carriage is not evidence our named source is wrong. I contest F14, because we do not build a published range on a Wikipedia total.

rulings.note: The article tells readers nobody can say what caused the flood when the cause has been publicly attributed for weeks. Failing to fetch one NDRRMA page is not the same as an absent record. The writer concedes and the ICIMOD and Kathmandu Post material is usable with attribution.

The frame that 5,285 exists only in the English wire is wrong on the facts, as the defence itself confirms after checking Nepali carriage. The corrected version, including that one outlet used both words for the same number, is stronger and must run.
The dek asserts an institutional failure to reconcile that the newsroom never tested. Only the provable claim may run: neither published update explains the difference.
The identification figures sit in the dispatch already cited and are the strongest verified facts available. Omitting them from a story about counting is a real gap.
Characterising three named newsrooms as not doing their own reporting, without naming the agency feed, is an unsourced swipe. Report the carriage, drop the judgement.
The lede and the cover card state 5,550 as settled while the headline rests on there being two counts. Self contradiction must go.

Basnet gave his account on the record to a national outlet under his own name. Two summary sentences with the outlet named and linked, adding nothing OnlineKhabar did not publish, is fair reuse, not exposure of a private person who never spoke.

"Told OnlineKhabar that" is indirect speech and claims no exact words. Putting quote marks around a translation would be the worse error. Name spelling follows the outlet's own Latin script, which the rules require.
A paragraph headed as a practical step for the diaspora that names no office, no place and no deadline cannot carry that framing.
Once F2 lands, the bookkeeping gap cannot carry the headline on the one month mark. The identification failure or Rasuwa cut off at day thirty is both truer and sharper.
An internal work log listing gaps on facts the article never prints is not journalism and wastes the close. Keep only disclosures that touch published claims.
An unnamed official is the sole source for the forward promise readers are told to watch. Attribute through Ratopati to the Army and say Ratopati did not name the officer, or pull the name.

Every sub total traces to Kantipur, a named source. Inability to find the same lines in a second carriage is not evidence of error. The optional Bidur or crop addition may run only with a named carriage.
The article's claim is narrow and accurate as corrected. A Wikipedia aggregate is not an NDRRMA count and cannot anchor a published range.

Sustained on the word count only. The body must come under 700 words. Overruled on the district list: the fifth district and the 15 local levels are not in any source the desk read and must not be printed unattributed.

judge_1.reason: As it stands the piece tells readers the cause of the flood is unknown when it has been publicly attributed for weeks, and it builds its headline and dek on a premise the defence itself has now disproved, that 5,285 lived only in the English wire. It also asserts an institutional failure it never tested and leaves the strongest verified number in its own source, 112 bodies identified, out entirely.
